archetypes.name: timing-env
archetypes.rationale: A1/A2 depend on exact timing-call enumeration, env-prefix placement, and implement-vs-review scope boundaries that static reviewers may not fully exhaust.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the A1/A2 timing-skill pin plan against the actual implement timing surfaces and launcher parity. Check whether the proposed scanner covers every production mark/report/vendor-task invocation without sweeping in /review or non-mark subcommands, and whether scope-files includes enough evidence for reviewers to verify the invariant. Pay special attention to same-line env-prefix requirements, multiline record-vendor-task calls, and polluted ambient design env cases. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: ci-outcomes
archetypes.rationale: B asks for narrowly targeted monitor-level outcome coverage, so a state-machine reviewer can catch duplicate tests or missing terminal branches before implementation.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the CI monitor testing plan for gaps between the requested monitor-level outcome coverage and the existing decide/evaluate/resume/counter test evidence. Verify that the candidate cases are genuinely uncovered, assert terminal MonitorResult/Outcome behavior rather than internal details, and avoid real gh/git execution by using the existing runner stubs. Flag any proposed test that duplicates parity-table coverage or misses a more relevant outcome branch. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: run-log-posture
archetypes.rationale: D combines retention filters, sidecar fixture coverage, comments, Python quiet-log posture, and SECURITY.md residual-risk wording where contract drift is easy.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the D1-D4 run-log plan for consistency between larch-log retention rules, write-round fixtures, dynamic Codex sidecar handling, and documented redaction posture. Check that the SECURITY.md update accurately frames pattern-based redaction as by-design residual risk without implying new controls, and that any sibling contract docs are updated only when they restate the changed rationale. Include the Python quiet-log append decision in the same contract-drift pass so documented operator expectations stay aligned across bash and Python paths. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
